ambition: Realize life and consciousness in a computational substrate while investigating whether and under what conditions this is possible.
rules: No behavioral milestone automatically certifies life or consciousness.
Preregister thresholds, duration, resource limits and controls before simulations.
Do not overwrite baseline graph weights; keep plastic changes separate.
Do not use external motor policies as final connectome-driven behavior.

tickets.title: Reproduce a published neural rhythm positive control
tickets.delivery: Run a small published CPG reference with its real IDs, weights, units and timing, plus no-input and E1/E2-cut controls.
acceptance: Pin paper revision, code revision, input units and weight orientation before execution.
Compare rhythm and recruitment to the matching source data; do not equate this with six-leg walking.
Keep the original full connectome unchanged and record CPU/time/memory budgets.

tickets.title: Demonstrate propulsion feasibility of the exact muscle-body model
tickets.delivery: Verify support, swing and propulsion using calibration drive on the exact body and muscle paths used by the research runtime.
acceptance: Use recorded kinematics or an explicitly diagnostic teacher; no root-position forcing.
Measure fore-aft contact impulse, stance slip, work, posture and net displacement.
Direct torque-only success does not certify the muscle model; keep diagnostic controls out of final autonomous runs.

tickets.title: Persist and account for physiological state in an experiment
tickets.delivery: Run a bounded internal-state trajectory with energy, hydration, damage, fatigue and sleep pressure, expose its accounting to the operator, and resume it exactly.
acceptance: Declare units, parameter sources and surrogate assumptions; reject nonfinite or impossible updates.
Account for basal cost, activity cost and explicit restoration events without creating energy from negative work.
Keep resource inputs and operator actions in a provenance log; verify split-run equivalence.
Do not label a viability variable as proof of life.

tickets.title: Couple internal needs to declared neural inputs
tickets.delivery: Compare neural responses to the same external stimulus under different physiological states using explicit interoceptive or neuromodulatory mappings.
acceptance: Record actual target neuron IDs and confidence of each mapping.
Motor decision code cannot read physiological scalars as an action lookup; operator telemetry may display them.
Include state-fixed and interoceptive-path-cut controls with matched random streams.
Treat unspecified peptide and receptor dynamics as assumptions, not measured physiology.

tickets.title: Connect ingestion actions to energy and water recovery
tickets.delivery: In a controlled feeding scene, neural/motor ingestion events transfer food or water into the internal-state model.
acceptance: Contact alone does not restore resources; require an evidenced ingestion action.
Track consumed amount, availability and state change with an accounting balance.
Use taste/ingestion pathway cuts and no-resource controls.
Complete a mouth-actuation positive control before claiming embodied feeding.

tickets.title: Retain an association through sparse local plasticity
tickets.delivery: Condition one identified mushroom-body compartment and retain an association after washout and checkpoint restoration.
acceptance: Whitelist actual KC-to-MBON edges and declared DAN modulation; preserve raw graph IDs and baseline weights.
Store sparse eligibility and memory deltas with bounds and no unintended sign flips.
Compare paired, unpaired, plasticity-off and memory-reset conditions.
Remove transient-state and testing-state differences when attributing an effect to memory.
A saved log alone does not count as learned memory.

tickets.title: Demonstrate state-dependent retrieval of food and water associations
tickets.delivery: Show how the same learned cues affect approach or ingestion differently under hunger and thirst.
acceptance: Test learned associations under matched histories and explicitly controlled physiological states.
Include memory-reset, state-fixed and modulation-cut controls.
Use actual neural/body actions, not an odor-to-action lookup table.
Separate short-lived adaptation from persistent associative effects.

tickets.title: Maintain viable internal ranges in held-out environments
tickets.delivery: Maintain declared energy and hydration ranges through neural-driven behavior in environments not used for calibration.
acceptance: Preregister viable ranges, duration, held-out seeds and effect-size thresholds before trials.
Compare live interoception with matched cuts and no-resource controls.
Measure time within range, recovery and resource use; do not use an external destination command.
Do not infer life or consciousness from passing this functional benchmark.

tickets.title: Test learned self-maintenance and divergent individual histories
tickets.delivery: Train matched A/B instances with different cue outcomes, restore them into controlled test conditions, and compare learned hazard avoidance and viability.
acceptance: Keep initial graph/model constant; isolate memory from current energy, hydration, damage and random-state differences.
Compare naive, sham, unpaired, memory-reset and pathway-cut controls.
Measure predictive avoidance and viability duration, including predeclared resource-risk trade-offs.
Do not hardcode danger avoidance as the policy or automatically award a self-preservation flag.
Self-maintenance remains inside the simulated world; pause, reset and shutdown remain under operator control.

tickets.title: Establish a life and consciousness research evidence framework
tickets.delivery: Publish the project's explicit realization ambition, competing definitions/theories, measurable indicators, counterevidence and limits of interpretation.
acceptance: Retain life and consciousness as long-term goals rather than replacing them with behavioral milestones.
Separate functional tests, theory-dependent indicators and claims of actual realization.
Do not add a universal consciousness score or a boolean that treats passing behavior tests as proof.
Document what evidence would weaken each interpretation and how external review can challenge it.
Mark this issue as an initial research protocol, not completion of the life/consciousness goal.
